The job: understand a business before onboarding it.

A payments analyst needs to connect company names to evidence, untangle disclosed relationships, and identify missing ownership information. This workspace turns those steps into a reviewable case.

What the evidence actually supports

Disclosed relationship Percentages appear only when explicitly stated.
Research aid, not a completed KYB or beneficial-owner verification. Real companies shown are subjects of public records, not asserted customers of Aster Pay or Trulioo.

Add evidence to this case

Upload a text-based PDF, HTML filing or text file, or paste an excerpt. Files are processed in this browser and are not uploaded to a server. Scanned PDFs need OCR first.

Explicit ownership sentences and subsidiary tables are supported. Candidate extraction is deterministic; entity matching uses a trained model. Unsupported text stays available as evidence without invented relationships.

A working evidence investigation

Built for the analyst who needs to identify the correct legal entity, inspect corporate relationships and explain what remains unknown.

What is ML here?

A trained logistic entity matcher ranks name variants against the case evidence. Training, held-out evaluation and the exported model are included in the source package. Match scores are ranking signals, not identity verification probabilities. On the synthetic validation set, precision and recall are both 100%, but a simple edit-similarity baseline ties the model. This evaluation does not demonstrate an ML advantage or real-world accuracy.

What is deliberately constrained?

Document parsing recognizes explicit ownership sentences and subsidiary tables. It does not use an LLM or infer unseen owners. A subsidiary disclosure does not identify a direct parent, percentage, or ultimate human owner unless it says so.

Data & privacy

Public SEC filing facts are bundled as dated snapshots with source links. Uploads and notes stay in this browser tab. Export a brief before closing; the app has no shared case database. New documents are unverified analyst inputs.
